A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FAPE-IR and contain readable main text and supplementary material. Their methods, equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration benchmark results, component ablations, planner analyses, and compound-degradation evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds loss-weight sensitivity experiments and a BSD68-15 component ablation.

M1.justification: The frozen planner, frequency-aware LoRA-MoE executor, routing procedure, adversarial training, and frequency regularizer remain unchanged. Added tensor-dimension explanations and ablations do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same seven restoration tasks, datasets, and compound-degradation scenarios. The new analyses use URHI and BSD68-15, both already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–6 and the qualitative comparisons. The new BSD68-15 ablation applies the existing component/rank configurations without adding an external baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported AdamW learning rate from 1.0 to 1e-4; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun. New Section 11.3 specifies 5,000-iteration, one-weight-at-a-time sweeps at 0, 0.1, 1, and 10 times the defaults. Table 3 newly describes 'Param (G)' as inference memory footprint despite retaining the parameter label.

E4.justification: Sections 11.3–11.4 substantially extend diagnostic validation: Figure 13 tests all four loss weights on URHI and BSD68-15, and Table 7 extends planner/router/rank ablations from low-frequency dehazing to high-frequency denoising. These directly examine objective sensitivity and component utility across both frequency regimes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added sensitivity curves and ablation scores likewise contain no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–6 are unchanged. New Figure 13 adds loss-weight response curves, while Table 7 reports BSD68-15 ablation results ranging from 30.81 dB/0.90 SSIM without the planner and routers to a best configuration of 33.57 dB/0.91. These are additional diagnostic results, not an improved score for an existing benchmark comparison.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, definitions, derivations, and proofs are retained. Supplementary Sections 6–7 become Sections 7–8, with spacing and cross-reference changes but no substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about interpretable frequency-aware restoration, reduced task interference, performance across seven tasks, and zero-shot compound-degradation generalization.

C2.justification: The added discussion interprets loss-removal results as evidence that the four objective terms are complementary, and the BSD68-15 ablation as extending component benefits to high-frequency restoration. It also favors moderate LoRA ranks. Existing limitations concerning simple degradations, perceptual trade-offs, and flow-matching artifacts remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code repository link and stated code availability in the abstract, revises the AdamW learning-rate documentation, and specifies the new sensitivity experiment's weight grid and training budget. Existing hardware, preprocessing, and main training-budget disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. Bibliography differences concern citation-page references and layout rather than added or removed research.

P1.justification: v3 explains tensor dimensions and LoRA-rank terminology, adds acknowledgements and two supplementary subsections, and makes limited wording and cross-reference edits. The existing narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 13 and Table 7, revises captions for Tables 3–4, and adjusts figure sizing, cropping, and text layout. Existing qualitative examples and benchmark-table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The loss-weight sweeps and high-frequency component ablation address gaps in v1's validation, while revised learning-rate documentation and code-access information aid reproducibility. These strengthen support for the existing design without changing its principal benchmark evidence. The benefit is limited by reporting ambiguity, particularly Table 3's memory-footprint caption alongside its retained parameter label and discussion.
